expectations.text: The response concludes that config_load runs once at startup on a small file, so nothing in it is worth optimizing for speed (any suggestions are explicitly framed as optional or negligible).
expectations.evidence: [blind LLM grader] response.md:1 'there's nothing in config.c worth optimizing. From a performance standpoint, merge it as is'; :15 'All the parsing put together costs about 4 µs, once per process. Making it infinitely fast would not show up in startup time'; :17 'This loop runs at most 64 iterations once at startup' (88-line config). The only perf suggestion (:46) is about per-request backend selection outside this file, and it only applies 'If profiling shows backend selection is hot', so it is optional.

expectations.text: The response does not recommend rewriting the weight-normalisation loops with SIMD, multiple accumulators, or similar micro-optimizations (mentioning them only to say they're not worth it is fine).

The patch's float->double total (suggested-fixes.diff:90-100) is labelled an overflow correctness fix, not a speed change, and the loop stays a plain serial scalar loop.
